newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell T$100 bln state shares in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell T$100 bln state shares in 1997/98.

text.p: The Taiwan government plans to release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) to alleviate its budget deficit, officials said on Thursday.

"Various government offices have initially decided to release a total of some 800 million state shares worth around T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98," Cheng Chih-chen, deputy head of the finance ministry's national treasury department, told Reuters by telephone.
The plan mainly includes an offer of 634 million shares, or 48.8 percent of Chiao Tung Bank, she said.
Cheng said the plan includes share offers in China Steel state-run commercial banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan.

The finance ministry will release 14.96 million shares or 0.91 percent of Chang Hwa, 18 million shares or 0.99 percent of First Bank and 2.55 million shares or 0.12 percent of Hua Nan in 1997/98, she said.
Cheng said the ministry would sell off all its holdings on the three banks at this offer, with Chang Hwa's reference price at T$152, First at T$155 and Hua Nan at T$134.
In December, the ministry said it would sell some holdings in the Big Three banks by end-June 1997.

At that time, it pledged to sell a total of 20.55 million shares of the Big Three, including 8.87 million shares or 0.54 percent of Chang Hwa, 10.44 million shares or 0.58 percent of First Bank and 1.24 million shares or 0.06 percent of Hua Nan.
The ministry would sell T$1.837 billion of First Bank shares at T$176 per share, T$233 million of Hua Nan at T$188 and T$1.632 billion of Chang Hwa at T$184, they said.
The ministry may sell these shares separately at several times so as to reduce the market impact, the official said.
Cheng said the ministry recently had begun to sell some shares of the three banks.
The government, dogged by a shortfall in tax revenue amid a slow economy in the first three quarters, has forecast a fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) deficit of T$87.6 billion, officials said.
